newsitem.title: USA: Equitable strengthens reserves in Q4.
newsitem.headline: Equitable strengthens reserves in Q4.

text.p: Equitable Cos Inc said it strengthened reserves related primarily to its disability income business by $339.3 million in the fourth quarter.
The disability income actions are intended to eliminate losses from both direct and assumed businesses, which in 1996 together totaled $47.1 million after-tax, Equitable said
Equitable said it also strengthened reserves for its group pension and discontinued operations.

Equitable said it strengthened reserves for discontinued operations as a result of the quarterly review of the loss allowance and premium deficiency reserves for discontinued GIC contracts and wind-up annuities.
Future sales of real estate, and the related gains or losses, will impact the quarterly results of discontinued operations, Equitable said.
Fourth quarter after-tax operating earnings rose 46 percent to $138.2 million, or $0.64 per fully diluted share, which excludes after-tax investment gains and nonrecurring charges of $346.1 million.

This compares with after-tax operating earnings of $94.9 million, or 45 cents per fully diluted share, for the fourth quarter of 1995, which exclude after-tax investment losses and nonrecurring charges of $17.7 million.

Also during the final period of 1996, the company said it adopted FASB 120, which prescribes the accounting for certain individual participating life insurance contracts, most of which are included in the closed block book of business.
This new accounting treatment produces results which more closely reflect the economics of participating life contracts, Equitable said.

The application of FASB 120 resulted in increases in after-tax results of $19.2 million for 1996 and $15.2 million for 1995, as well as a $240.3 million aggregate increase in equity at December 31, 1996, Equitable said.
Prior year's results have been restated retroactively.
Also, the adoption of FASB 121 at the beginning of 1996 produced a $23.1 million after-tax charge to full year's results reflecting the cumulative effect of this change.
Following the actions, 1996 after-tax net income totaled $99.1 million, or 36 cents per fully diluted share, compared with $365.4 million, or $1.74 per fully diluted share in 1995.

Results for 1996 also include after-tax investment losses of $7.2 million -- net of deferred acquisition cost (DAC) amortization and related costs -- and after-tax restructuring charges of $15.1 million, primarily in connection with the consolidation of most insurance service center operations to one facility.
Results for 1995 include after-tax investment gains of $11.3 million -- net of DAC and related costs -- and after-tax restructuring charges of $25.4 million.
"On the insurance side, we continued to build sales and earnings momentum, and our investment companies once again turned in outstanding performances," Equitable chief executive Joseph Melone said.
"We also took aggressive actions to deal with some old problems, which have somewhat obscured the significant progress The Equitable has made in recent years," he said.
"With these actions and the strong fundamentals of all our core businesses, we are very optimistic about our operating prospects for 1997," Melone said.

Fourth quarter after-tax operating earnings for Equitable's insurance and annuity operations rose 66 percent to $71.2 million, excluding after-tax investment gains of $2.1 million -- net of DAC and related expenses -- after-tax restructuring charges of $12.7 million and after-tax reserve strengthening of $255.5 million.
This compares with after-tax operating earnings of $42.9 million, which exclude after-tax investment losses of $14.5 million and after-tax restructuring charges of $13.3 million.

"Central to these higher results was strong growth in variable assets and widening spreads on our general account annuity business," said James M. Benson, chief executive officer of The Equitable Life Assurance Society.
